records.place: Stenimachos, Naoussa PDO, Imathia, Central Macedonia, Greece

wine.name: Grande Reserve Naoussa
wine.classification: Grande Reserve, the Greek term for a red aged at least four years before release
wine.grapes: Xinomavro alone, as the Naoussa appellation requires.
wine.sites: Selected vineyards across the Naoussa appellation on the south eastern foothills of Mount Vermio, picked and vinified plot by plot, by the house's account, and blended only at the end of the barrel ageing.
wine.making: Fermented in stainless steel with about a week on the skins, then put through malolactic fermentation. The wine spends two years in French oak barrels and two more in bottle in the house's cellars at Naoussa before it is released, four years in all.
wine.glass: Garnet turning brick at the rim; dried cherry, cinnamon and cedar from the barrel over sun dried tomato, dried rose and leather; medium in body, with lively acidity and firm, drying tannin that the years have begun to soften.
wine.ageing: Released after four years and ready to drink then; a good vintage keeps for a decade and more, turning towards leather and dried fruit.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant an older bottle gently off its sediment; a Burgundy or Nebbiolo style glass.

label.means: The protected appellation on the slopes of Mount Vermio, red only and Xinomavro alone.
The Greek ageing term for a PDO red held at least four years before release.
The grape, whose name means acid black, for its sharp acidity and dark skin.

records.table: Boutari's Grande Reserve Naoussa is the old school Naoussa: Xinomavro alone, two years in French oak and two in bottle before release. It smells of dried cherry, cinnamon and sun dried tomato, with firm tannin and bright acidity, so pour it beside roast lamb.
records.story: The house began at Naoussa in 1879, when its founder set up the winery that carries the family name. In 1906 the company opened a winery and cellar of its own in the town, by its own account the first in private hands there, and launched the bottled red labelled Naoussa Boutari; a separate account credits the founder with selling wine in glass bottles when most Greek wine went out in demijohns and skins. The founder's son took over in the middle of the 1930s and opened the first export markets, among them Austria, Hungary and Egypt. When Greece drew up its first appellations in 1971, Naoussa was among them, Xinomavro alone and red only. In 1978 the house opened a new winery at Stenimachos, outside the town, which has been the centre of its making, bottling and ageing ever since. The Grande Reserve was the house's answer to a longer Naoussa: grapes from selected vineyards, kept apart plot by plot, and four years of ageing, half of it in French oak, before release. The company grew into a national group with estates on Santorini, at Mantinia, at Goumenissa and on Crete, and in 2022 it was sold to an investment group. For a sommelier the Grande Reserve is the reference for the traditional, long aged style of Naoussa.

others.name: Naoussa Boutari
others.note: The house's younger Naoussa, the bottled red first launched in 1906 and the wine that carried the name abroad.

others.name: 1879 Boutari Legacy

traps: Boutari and Kir-Yianni are separate companies; Kir-Yianni was founded in 1997 by a member of the Boutari family after he left the family firm.
Grande Reserve is a legal ageing term in Greece, at least four years for a red, not a house brand or a vineyard name.
The house's Goumenissa, Mantinia and Cretan wines come from its other estates; only the Xinomavro of the Naoussa appellation may be labelled Naoussa.

questions.exp: The 1906 cellar launched Naoussa Boutari, by the house's own history; the Grande Reserve came later, and Ramnista and Paliokalias belong to other houses.

report: The founder is described, not named: his dates could not be found in any source, and the brief names the long dead only with dates.
The house's page and two reviews agree on two years in French oak and two in bottle; one retailer's promise of a decade in the cellars was left out.
The 1906 first bottled red is the house's claim; a separate press account dates glass bottles to 1879, so both are hedged.

No source gives the first vintage of the Grande Reserve, so the story gives none; the Grande Reserve minimum in Greek law is given as four years for a red, the split between cask and bottle varying by source and left out.
The region record names the founder Ioannis Boutaris with 1879; the record keeps the year and describes the man.

wine.name: Ramnista
wine.grapes: Xinomavro alone, as the Naoussa appellation requires.
wine.sites: Blocks of the estate's vineyard at Yianakohori on the eastern slopes of Mount Vermio, at about 250 to 350 metres, on light sandy loam and sandy clay with some lime, by the estate's fact sheets.
wine.making: The wine is aged in French oak barrels of 225 and 500 litres, a share of them new, for about fourteen to eighteen months according to the vintage, then bottled and held at the estate before release.
wine.glass: Sour cherry, plum and dried rose with tomato leaf and black olive, a little clove and toast from the barrel; medium bodied, with vivid acidity and firm, fine grained tannin that recalls Nebbiolo.
wine.ageing: Firm in its first years; a good vintage opens after five or six and keeps for well over a decade.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour or more; a Burgundy or Nebbiolo style glass.

label.means: Ktima means estate: the house founded at Yianakohori in 1997.
A local name for the estate's rolling hills, read by the house as royal hill.
The protected appellation of Imathia, red only and Xinomavro alone.

records.table: Ramnista is Kir-Yianni's Naoussa, Xinomavro alone from the estate's hills at Yianakohori, aged in French barrels of two sizes. It gives sour cherry, tomato leaf and dried rose with firm, fine tannin, so decant it and pour it with lamb or mushrooms.
records.story: The land came first. In 1968 a member of the Boutari family bought a plot outside Yianakohori, a village of the Naoussa district, and planted it with Xinomavro, and with Merlot beside it. Its fruit went into the family firm's wines, and in 1995 the first bottles under the estate's own name reached the market as Boutari Estate in Yianakohori, a blend of Xinomavro with Merlot. Then he left the family business and in 1997 founded Kir-Yianni at Yianakohori, its first vintage made entirely in the new winery that year; the house later added vineyards at Amyndeon, higher and cooler to the west. By the house's own account Ramnista was the first wine of the new estate. Its name is a local one for the rolling hills of the vineyard: the house reads it as royal hill, and also tells that the slope was overgrown with buckthorn before it was planted again. Ramnista is aged in French barrels of 225 and 500 litres rather than in the large old casks of the district's older cellars. For a sommelier it is the modern, structured Naoussa that keeps the grape's acid and tannin.

others.name: Diaporos
others.note: The estate's single vineyard red from its Naoussa blocks, a firmer and longer aged wine than Ramnista.

others.name: Samaropetra
others.note: A white from Amyndeon, Roditis with Sauvignon Blanc.

traps: Kir-Yianni and Boutari are separate companies of one family origin; Ramnista is Kir-Yianni's wine, never Boutari's.
Ramnista is Naoussa PDO, Xinomavro alone; the house's Kali Riza is Amyndeon, a different appellation further west.
The Yianakohori estate wine of 1995 was a Xinomavro and Merlot blend; Ramnista is Xinomavro alone.

cards.front: What is Ramnista, and which house makes it?
cards.back: Kir-Yianni's Naoussa: Xinomavro alone from the estate's hills at Yianakohori, aged in French oak.

cards.front: In which year was the land of the Yianakohori estate bought?

questions.q: A guest asks what grapes are in Kir-Yianni's Ramnista. What do you tell them?
questions.exp: Ramnista is Naoussa PDO, which allows Xinomavro alone; Negoska belongs in Goumenissa's blend, and the estate's 1995 wine with Merlot was a different label.

questions.q: Kir-Yianni was founded at Yianakohori in 1997. What had its founder done just before?
questions.exp: A member of the Boutari family left the family business and founded Kir-Yianni on land bought in 1968; the Amyndeon vineyards were added, not closed.

report: The house's pages disagree on whether Ramnista was first launched in 1996 or with the founding of 1997, so no first vintage is given; the story says only that it was the first wine of the new estate, by the house's account.
The barrel time moves by vintage (18 months for 2015, 16 for 2016, 14 for 2020 on the house's sheet), so the record gives a range.
A press notice suggests the founder died in November 2024 or 2025; he stays unnamed, as people.json lists him, and the integrator may wish to check and name him with his dates.
Samaropetra's grapes and Diaporos as a single vineyard rest on the library and the house's pages respectively.

records.place: Trilofos, Naoussa PDO, Imathia, Central Macedonia, Greece

wine.name: Earth and Sky
wine.grapes: Xinomavro alone, from vines of about forty five years.
wine.sites: Parcels around Trilofos, at 150 to 250 metres on the south eastern edge of the appellation, for about seven tenths, and around Fytia, at 450 to 650 metres, where the wide swing between day and night adds freshness, for the rest.
wine.making: The vineyards are farmed organically and certified, with biodynamic methods. The grapes are fermented with wild yeasts, and the wine is aged for eighteen months in French oak barrels of 500 litres in their third use, so the wood frames the fruit without marking it.
wine.glass: Dark cherry, strawberry and blackberry with black slate, dried tomato skin, tea and a wisp of smoke; fuller and riper than the old school, with fresh acidity and powerful but silky tannin.
wine.ageing: Open and generous within a few years of release; a strong vintage gains over seven to ten years and more.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Burgundy or Nebbiolo style glass.

label.means: Earth and Sky in Greek, the name the wine carries on its Greek label.
The protected appellation of Imathia, red only and Xinomavro alone.
The family's village at the south eastern edge of Naoussa, where most of the vines grow.

records.table: Thymiopoulos Earth and Sky, Gi kai Ouranos in Greek, is the house's old vine Naoussa: Xinomavro from Trilofos and the higher slopes of Fytia, farmed organically and raised in large, used French barrels. It is riper and silkier than the old school, so serve it a touch cool.
records.story: Naoussa had been one of Greece's first appellations since 1971, red only and Xinomavro alone. The Thymiopoulos family had grown grapes and other crops at Trilofos, a village at the south eastern edge of the Naoussa appellation, for generations. The change came when a son of the family began to make wine from the family vineyards while he studied oenology, the first of them to do so. In 2005, by the house's own account, he made the first wine under the family name and called it Earth and Sky, Gi kai Ouranos in Greek. It drew on the family's old Xinomavro vines around Trilofos and on higher parcels around Fytia, up on the slopes of Mount Vermio, and it was raised in large, used French barrels. The vineyards were turned over to organic farming, certified, and worked with biodynamic methods. Alongside it the house made a Young Vines Xinomavro that showed the grape could be drunk young, and it went on to make wine at Rapsani on Mount Olympus under a company of its own, Terra Olympus. Its range grew to ten expressions of Xinomavro. For a sommelier Earth and Sky is the riper, gentler face of modern Naoussa, built on the grape's acidity.

others.name: Xinomavro Young Vines
others.note: The early drinking Xinomavro, called Jeunes Vignes abroad, the wine that showed the grape could be poured young.

others.name: Naoussa Alta
others.note: A Naoussa from a high block on schist near Fytia.

others.name: Terra Petra
others.note: The Rapsani red of Terra Olympus, the house's company on Mount Olympus, told with the Rapsani group.

traps: Earth and Sky is Naoussa PDO, Xinomavro alone; the house's Terra Petra is Rapsani, a three grape blend from Mount Olympus.
Earth and Sky and Gi kai Ouranos are one wine, the English and the Greek names on two labels.
Xinomavro Young Vines is the house's early drinking wine, not a second wine of Earth and Sky.

wine.name: Paliokalias
wine.sites: The Paliokalias vineyard, a traditional vineyard area on the eastern foothills of Mount Vermio a few kilometres south east of the town, at about 250 to 300 metres, farmed organically since 1996.
wine.making: Fermented in stainless steel with indigenous yeasts, then aged for about a year in French oak barrels, some of them of 300 litres and only a small share new. It is bottled without fining or filtration, with very little sulphur.
wine.glass: Sour cherry, cranberry and dried rose with sun dried tomato, black olive and a savoury, herb scented lift; pale and fine in texture, with high acidity and firm, chalky tannin.
wine.ageing: Tight in youth; it opens after five years or so and keeps for fifteen and more in a good vintage.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Burgundy or Nebbiolo style glass.

label.means: The name of the vineyard area south east of Naoussa town from which the wine comes.
The protected appellation of Imathia, red only and Xinomavro alone.
The grape, whose name means acid black, for its sharp acidity and dark skin.

records.table: Paliokalias is Dalamara's single vineyard Naoussa, old vine Xinomavro from the foothills south east of the town, farmed organically and bottled unfiltered. It is pale, perfumed and firm, with sour cherry, dried rose and olive, so give it air and serve it with lamb.
records.story: The Dalamara family counts its wine history in Naoussa from 1840, when, as the family tells it, an ancestor planted his first vineyard there; a contract of purchase from that time survives. For generations the family made wine and distilled spirits in the town, and its cellar and distillery stand at the edge of the town on the road out of Naoussa. When Greece drew up its first appellations in 1971, Naoussa was among them, red only and Xinomavro alone. The family turned its vineyards to organic farming in 1996, certified, opened the cellar to visitors in 1998 and began to work with biodynamic methods from 2008. Then came the change that made the house known abroad: a younger generation took over the cellar and with the 2009 vintage bottled the old vines of Paliokalias apart for the first time, as a single vineyard wine. It is made with wild yeasts, aged in older French barrels and bottled unfiltered, a lighter touch than the long cask ageing of the old Naoussa houses. For a sommelier Paliokalias is the perfumed, site driven Naoussa: a family cellar of the town letting one vineyard speak.

others.name: Dalamara Naoussa
others.note: The house's estate Naoussa, Xinomavro from its other parcels, aged longer in French oak.

traps: Paliokalias is the name of a vineyard area, not a grape or a style; the wine is Xinomavro alone, as Naoussa requires.
Dalamara's family history reaches back to 1840, but the single vineyard Paliokalias was first bottled apart with the 2009 vintage.

cards.front: Dalamara's Paliokalias: what is its vineyard, and how is it farmed?
cards.back: A vineyard area on the eastern foothills of Mount Vermio south east of Naoussa, at about 250 to 300 metres, farmed organically since 1996.

cards.front: With which vintage was Paliokalias first bottled apart as a single vineyard wine?

Four years in old Greek casks

questions.exp: Paliokalias is fermented with indigenous yeasts, aged about a year in mostly older French barrels and bottled unfined and unfiltered; its paleness is Xinomavro's own colour, not a light making.

questions.q: From which year does the Dalamara family count its wine history in Naoussa?
questions.exp: The family dates its first vineyard to 1840; 1879 is Boutari's founding, 1971 the year of the first Greek appellations and 1996 the start of its organic farming.

report: Founded stays empty: 1840 is the family's account of its first vineyard (Wines of Greece, from the family, and the Greek Gastronomy Guide), not a founding of the winery; the story tells it as the family's.
The family's purchase of the Paliokalias vineyard in the 1960s rests on one usable source (a second is a living writer's site), so it is left out.
The 2009 first single vineyard bottling rests on Kudos Wines and Wine With Seth; VOS gives 2011 as the year the son made the wine entirely, so the refuter may wish to test the date.
The ancestor of 1840 is described, not named, as no source gives his dates; the son who took over is living and unnamed.
The Wines of Greece English page speaks of the fifth generation, other sources of the sixth, so the record says a younger generation.

wine.name: Karydas Naoussa
wine.grapes: Xinomavro alone, from the family's own vines.
wine.sites: The family vineyard at Ano Gastra, about two and a half kilometres outside Naoussa at some 200 metres, on sandy clay; the vines were planted from 1980.
wine.making: The grapes are cold soaked for several days and fermented in stainless steel; the malolactic fermentation follows in concrete tanks, and the wine then ages for about a year and a half in French oak barrels, a share of them new, before bottling.
wine.glass: Red cherry and redcurrant with sun dried tomato, dried rose and a touch of cinnamon and vanilla from the barrel; medium bodied, with bright acidity and firm, fine tannin.
wine.ageing: Firm when young; it settles after four or five years and keeps for a decade and more in a good vintage.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Burgundy or Nebbiolo style glass.

label.means: Karydas Estate in Greek: the family's own vineyard and cellar at Ano Gastra.
The protected appellation of Imathia, red only and Xinomavro alone.
The grape, whose name means acid black, for its sharp acidity and dark skin.

records.table: Karydas Naoussa is a small family estate's Xinomavro, grown on its own vines at Ano Gastra above the town and aged in French oak. It shows cherry, sun dried tomato and dried rose with bright acid and firm tannin, a grower's Naoussa for roast meats.
records.story: Karydas is a grower's house, small and family run. The family planted its Xinomavro at Ano Gastra, a few kilometres outside the town of Naoussa on sandy clay, from 1980. In 1994 it built a small winery on the estate and began to make and bottle its own wine, and a son of the founder joined the house. When Greece drew up its first appellations in 1971 Naoussa was among them, red only and Xinomavro alone, and the Karydas Naoussa keeps to that rule: one grape from one family vineyard, fermented in steel, put through its malolactic fermentation in concrete and aged in French oak. The house made its name abroad with this Naoussa, which found importers in the United States, Britain and Germany. It also makes a second red, the Syllektiko, which adds a little Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon to Xinomavro and so falls outside the appellation. For a sommelier Karydas is the example of the small grower in Naoussa: a single estate, a single grape and the appellation in its plain form.

others.name: Syllektiko
others.note: The house's collection red, Xinomavro with a little Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, aged about two years in barrel; not a Naoussa.

traps: The Karydas Naoussa is Xinomavro alone; the house's Syllektiko adds Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon and so cannot carry the Naoussa name.
Karydas is a small family estate at Ano Gastra, not a merchant buying grapes across the district.

cards.front: Karydas Naoussa: where are its vines, and on what soil?
cards.back: At Ano Gastra, a few kilometres outside Naoussa, on sandy clay; the vines were planted from 1980.

cards.front: In which year did the Karydas family build its winery and begin to bottle its own wine?
cards.back: 1994, when it built a small winery on its estate at Ano Gastra.

questions.q: Which step of the Karydas Naoussa's making takes place in concrete tanks?
opts: The cold soak of the grapes
questions.exp: The grapes are cold soaked and fermented in stainless steel; the malolactic fermentation follows in concrete, and the ageing is in French oak barrels.

questions.q: The Karydas family planted its Xinomavro at Ano Gastra from 1980. When did it begin to bottle its own wine?
questions.exp: The winery was built on the estate in 1994 and the family's own wine began then; 1971 is the year of the Naoussa appellation, not of the house.

report: The plan's 1992 first vintage was found in one retailer only; Wines of Greece, Wine With Seth and Tacoma Wine Merchants give 1994 for the winery and the first wine, so founded is 1994.

The region record calls Karydas a one wine grower; it also makes the Syllektiko blend with Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon (two retailers), so the record teaches the Naoussa as its main wine, not its only one, and the region record wants a word changed.
The plan's village Gastra is Ano Gastra in Wines of Greece and Wine With Seth.
